sentences.text: Excellencies, distinguished colleagues, I hereby declare open the fifth meeting of the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council.
Excellencies, dear participants, we shall now continue the interactive dialogue with the independent expert on the promotion of a democratic and equitable international order.
According to our practice, We start by hearing the delegation of the country concerned by the report.
I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Iceland.
You have five minutes.
Thank you, Mr. President.
On the occasion, we have not prepared the specific remark, but thank you so much.
Thank you.
I now invite interested delegations to ask questions to the independent expert and to make comments on his report.
The speaking time is one minute 30 seconds for all.
So now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Venezuela on behalf of a group of countries.
Gracias. Thank you, Vice-President.
We make this statement on behalf of the Group of Friends in Defense of the UN Charter.

topics.label: Charter-Based Multilateralism
topics.description: A central theme was the defense of a UN-centered international order based on the Charter, sovereign equality, non-interference, dialogue, and international law. Delegations stressed that genuine multilateralism is the preferred alternative to unilateralism, coercion, and hegemonic power politics.

sentences.text: The group reaffirms its unbreakable commitment to the safeguard and the full observance of the principles and purposes enshrined in the UN Charter.

sentences.text: These are the foundation of a democratic, equitable international order based on, among other things, sovereign equality among states, non-intervention in internal matters, and the right for all people to self-determination, sovereignty, and permanent sovereignty over their wealth, natural resources, and the maintenance of peace.

topics.label: Double Standards in International Law
topics.description: Many interventions criticized selective application, politicization, and unequal enforcement of international law and human rights standards. The repeated call was for equal accountability, consistent application of norms, and an end to using human rights or sanctions selectively for political pressure.

topics.label: Global Regulatory Delivery Index
topics.description: The proposed voluntary global index to assess how states deliver on human rights and development commitments was a recurring topic. Supporters emphasized that any such tool should be non-prescriptive, account for structural constraints, and never be used for rankings or conditionality.

topics.label: South-South and Triangular Cooperation
